**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days are make-or-break for retention; nothing documented on initial class booking, induction safety checks, coach intro, goal-setting, or follow-up cadence
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no protocol for pause requests, win-back outreach, or exit interviews; members likely sliding away unnoticed
- **Member Checkins** – no scheduled touchpoint process (30/60/90-day); retention suffers without structured engagement points
- **Referral Programme** – no mechanism to systematize word-of-mouth or incentivize advocates
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – coaching consistency unmeasured; no standard for cue quality, form correction, music, pacing, energy
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – ambiguity on admin, prep, client comms—likely duplicated effort or things falling through
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – UK-based gym with payment/health data; legal and reputational risk unaddressed
- **Order Supplies & Sundries** – no documented reorder points, vendor contacts, or approval workflow; reactive vs. planned
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – common member complaints (injuries, class times, billing, equipment) have no standard resolution path

**Needs updating**

- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – likely vague on progression criteria, pay bands, or competency milestones; coaches unsure of growth path
- **30 Day Goals & Member Outcomes** – tracking process unclear; goals probably set but not reviewed; no tie to retention or upsell
- **Milestone Achievements** – celebration/recognition logic missing; demotivates members who hit targets silently
- **Transformation Pillars** – probably descriptive but not operationalized; no link to coaching practice

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Action Plan

## 🚨 SINGLE BIGGEST PRIORITY
**July revenue collapsed to £1,363 — a 92% drop from June (£17,711).** This is NOT a seasonality blip; it signals a catastrophic operational failure (likely a booking/billing system issue, data error, or summer closure). **Verify immediately:** are members still attending? Is the payment system processing? Is this a data recording error? Fix this before any strategic work.

---

## INCREASE REVENUE

• **Pricing audit & tier uplift:** Your ACRM (average revenue per member) is volatile (£120–£171) and trending downward in recent months (£120 in June). Implement tiered membership (Essential £35/month, Premium £55/month with PT/classes, VIP £75/month) and move existing members up where usage justifies it. This could unlock 15–20% revenue uplift without acquisition.

• **Recover lost members aggressively:** Churn spiked in April (8.33%), May (5.74%), and March (6.60%) post-relocation — members may have drifted. Launch a **"welcome back" campaign** with a free week for lapsed members (you had 147 in June, now 151 in July, but July revenue suggests they're not paying). Target the 40+ members who've churned since April.

• **December playbook—repeat it.** December hit £21,134 revenue and 49.54% profit margin with 124 members. That's your benchmark. Reverse-engineer what drove it: New Year's resolutions campaign, gift memberships, group training offers. Run the same campaign in October–November ahead of New Year (prep in August/September now).

• **Upsell PT and classes:** Non-membership revenue is invisible in your KPIs. Bundle 4 personal training sessions (£40–60 each) or unlimited class passes (£25/month add-on) to boost ACRM from £120 to £150+.

---

## REDUCE EXPENSES

• **Non-people costs are the leak:** June non-people expenses were £9,390 on £17,711 revenue (53% of turnover). May was £9,233 on £20,199 (46%). Even excluding April's relocation, this ratio is high. **Audit immediately:** rent/utilities, insurance, software, cleaning, laundry. Target is sub-40% of revenue. Negotiate rent with landlord (bigger studio should allow volume discount) or audit supplier contracts (software, insurance renewals).

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit current offering in 48 hours** — Have Grace walk the gym floor with a notebook. What classes run? What 1-on-1 options exist? What are members actually asking for? Don't rely on memory. This is your raw inventory.

• **Price from competitor teardown + value gap** — Mystery-shop 3-4 Belfast women's gyms. Screenshot their pricing. Now identify what The Forge does *differently* (community vibe? Female coaches? Programming specifics?). Price 10-15% premium to their baseline, justified by that difference. Don't undercut.

• **Build two separate one-pagers** — Coaches get a back-of-house version (revenue per service, what's bundled, upsell sequences). Members get a simple visual menu (classes/times, PT packages, add-ons like nutrition coaching). Use bright design — make it feel premium, not a PDF afterthought.

• **Test pricing with 5 existing members this week** — Sit down with your strongest advocates. Show them the menu. Ask: "Would you recommend this to a friend? Does this feel fair?" Adjust before it's official.

• **Hard-launch on socials + in-gym posters Friday** — One clear graphic per platform. QR code to full details. Physical copies at reception. Make it impossible to miss. This creates urgency and clarity simultaneously.

What's her biggest current confusion point — pricing tiers or what to actually include in packages?

# The Forge — Fractional CFO Report

## REVENUE — URGENT: Churn spike & pricing gap

• **May churn exploded to 12.8% (vs 3.5% June baseline).** That's 17 members lost that month alone. Root cause: post-relocation friction, pricing resistance, or class scheduling? Audit May joiners & leavers by cohort immediately. You've recovered to 142 active members by July, but May lost £2,000+ in lifetime value. **Action: Win back 5–8 churned May members with a 1-month free trial + schedule survey. Target: <5% monthly churn going forward.**

• **Rev/member is stuck at £120–£131 across 6 months (£18,472 annual contract value).** July hit £139 — that's your ceiling and only 3 months of data. You're leaving money on the table. **Action: Test price increase from current (assume ~£50/month base) to £60/month on new joiners next month. Model 2–3% sign-up dip; the revenue uplift is £840/month if you hold 140 members.**

• **July revenue hit £19.8k — your 6-month high.** Active base also highest (142). **Action: analyse July: what drove it? (New class, promo, seasonal fitness boom?) Replicate in Sept/Oct before Q4 New Year prep.**

• **No new revenue lines visible.** PT sessions, nutrition coaching, retail, class passes (non-members) aren't mentioned. **Action: Launch one PT package in Q4 at £25/session (3-session block £70). Target 4–6 clients × 2 sessions/month = £560–£840 monthly add-on within 90 days.**

---

## EXPENSES — Cash burn in March & April masks a baseline cost problem

• **Excluding April relocation, your baseline monthly cash out is £16.5k–£20.6k against £14k–£19.8k revenue.** You're running thin margins or carrying hidden overhead. **Call-out: June cash out (£20.6k) nearly doubled June revenue (£15.8k) — that's a red flag.** Are lease, payroll, or supplier payments bunching? **Action: Itemise June and May cash out by category (payroll, rent, utilities, suppliers, contractors). Identify any one-off payments masking true monthly run-rate. Target: cash out should consistently sit 15–20% *below* revenue once you've stabilised at 140+ members.**
